title: Representation Amendment (6 Regions Per State, 2 Senators Per Region) Bill 2020
short_title: Representation Amendment (6 Regions Per State, 2 Senators Per Region) Bill 2020

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would replace statewide Senate electorates with six electoral regions in each state, with each region represented by two senators in Parliament.
The minister would determine regional divisions, while half-Senate elections would elect senators for three regions rather than six senators across the whole state.
Transition rules would allow the President of the Senate to draw lots to select three regions if the first election were a half-Senate election.
changes: A state's capital city area would have to fit wholly within one region.
No region could cover more than 30% of its state's geographical area.
Existing Senate representation requirements in the Representation Act would be removed.
summary.affected: State voters, senators, the responsible minister and the President of the Senate are affected.
